### 💡 Codex Review https://github.com/AhmedMahmoud2222/DCIM/blob/c3324e4182095b6350daf5773ac48b9e00c0d226/backend/backend/tests/integration/test_cooling_concurrency.py#L90 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Identify the specific request and blocker when detecting a waiter** When another session on the PostgreSQL cluster is waiting on a matching statement, this query can release the test gate before the request under test reaches its intended lock. It filters neither database nor request PID nor blocking backend; the second test even accepts any blocked `FOR UPDATE`. Consequently, an unrelated waiter can make interleaving A pass without exercising the original deadlock, or make interleaving B pass without retirement actually waiting behind the relationship insertion. Correlate the observed waiter with the tested request and verify its blocker, rather than accepting a cluster-wide statement match. --- https://github.com/AhmedMahmoud2222/DCIM/blob/c3324e4182095b6350daf5773ac48b9e00c0d226/backend/backend/tests/integration/test_cooling_concurrency.py#L138-L140 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Cancel and await request tasks on exceptional test exits** If either synchronization wait times out, or the test is cancelled, this `finally` only releases the gate: the exception skips the subsequent `gather`, leaving the request tasks running. The second new test similarly skips `await retire_task` when waiter detection fails. `concurrent_client()` restores dependency overrides and disposes its engine but does not cancel or join these independently created tasks, so requests can outlive their test context and retain transactions or interfere with teardown. Track all created tasks and cancel and await unfinished ones in an outer `finally`, including timeout and cancellation paths.
